shortName: Methodist University Cape Fear Valley Health School of Medicine
additionalCoursework: MU CFVH does not require any specific prerequisite coursework. Applicants may view an additional list of suggested coursework here: https://www.methodist.edu/academics/medicine/admissions/suggested-coursework/.

medSchoolStudLife.diversity: Beyond Academics provides a wide range of support programs to help students succeed personally and professionally. These include academic coaching, peer tutoring, career advising, financial literacy resources, mentorship opportunities, and accommodations services. Our team is dedicated to connecting students with the tools and guidance they need to navigate challenges, build confidence, and thrive throughout their medical school journey.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: Student organizations give future physicians the chance to connect, lead, and grow outside the classroom. From interest groups in medical specialties to service, wellness, and cultural organizations, students can explore their passions while building community with their peers. These groups provide opportunities for leadership, collaboration, and professional development, while also reflecting the school’s commitment to service and engagement with southeastern North Carolina. Together, our students create a vibrant campus life that supports both personal and professional growth.
medSchoolStudLife.setting: The Methodist University Cape Fear Valley Health School of Medicine is located in Fayetteville, North Carolina, within the Cape Fear Valley Health System—the region’s leading healthcare provider. Our setting offers students a unique opportunity to learn in a diverse community that includes both rural and urban populations, with strong ties to military families and underserved communities. With direct access to Cape Fear Valley Medical Center and affiliated clinics, students experience early clinical exposure, community engagement, and a supportive environment that reflects our mission to improve health outcomes in southeastern North Carolina and beyond.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: Students have access to a variety of housing options in and around Fayetteville, NC. From modern apartments near Cape Fear Valley Medical Center to quiet neighborhoods and student-friendly communities close to campus, students can find a living arrangement that fits their needs and lifestyle. Fayetteville offers an affordable cost of living, convenient amenities, and proximity to shopping, dining, and outdoor activities. The Student Experience Office provides guidance and resources to help students secure safe, comfortable housing as they begin their medical school journey.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: MU CFVH is committed to fostering an inclusive, affirming environment for all students. Gender and sexual minority students have access to dedicated support systems, including confidential counseling, student affinity groups, and mentorship opportunities with faculty and community leaders. Our policies uphold equity and belonging, while our Student Services team actively works to connect students with resources, advocacy networks, and safe spaces. We are dedicated to ensuring that every student feels respected, supported, and empowered to thrive academically and personally.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystemsForDisabilities: MU CFVH is committed to providing equal educational opportunities for persons with disabilities in accordance with the nondiscrimination policy of MU CFVH SOM and in compliance with Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, with Title II of the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990, and with the ADA Amendments Act of 2008. Applicants who have questions about accessibility services can reach out to MUSOM_SAAS@methodist.edu.
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms: Student well-being is at the heart of our mission. MU CFVH offers comprehensive wellness programs and resources designed to support students physically, emotionally, and socially throughout their medical journey. From confidential behavioral health services and stress management workshops to fitness facilities, peer support networks, and access and accommodations services, we prioritize holistic wellness. Our goal is to ensure students thrive both in and out of the classroom, preparing them to become resilient, compassionate physician leaders.
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: At the Methodist University Cape Fear Valley Health School of Medicine, our campus culture is built on collaboration, inclusion, and community. Students are welcomed into a supportive environment where  belonging is at the heart of the student experience. Small class sizes, close faculty mentorship, and active student organizations foster meaningful connections, while service-learning and community engagement create opportunities to make a real difference in southeastern North Carolina. Our students don’t just learn medicine—they grow as compassionate leaders committed to improving health outcomes and advancing equity in the communities they serve.
medSchoolStudLife.transportationAdditionalInfo: Students may be required to travel to multiple sites for any clinical experience or other required learning activities and must have a reliable means of transportation.  Should a student choose not to own a vehicle, they are still responsible for arriving at sites on time. Schedules will not be adjusted due to transportation concerns.

medSchoolCurriculum.dressCode: Professional attire is expected in clinical environments: business casual with white coats for patient care; scrubs for skills workshops and designated clinical rotations.
medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: The Center for Academic and Professional Excellence (CAPE) provides individualized academic support, including tutoring. Faculty and leadership all have office hours.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: MS1–MS2 students build skills through interactive clinical, simulation, and ultrasound sessions, then advance to high-quality patient-care settings in MS3–MS4.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: The pre-clerkship curriculum uses a flipped-classroom model with modified team-based learning, case-driven sessions, and labs. Clinical rotations provide integrated and advanced clinical experiences.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Clinical rotations in the CFVH system offer all students high-quality training experiences.  CFVH is a regional academic trauma center with residency and fellowship programs in multiple specialties.
medSchoolCurriculum.prematriculationProgram: A one-week program will be offered to all students prior to orientation, aiming to develop students’ study techniques through hands-on practice and real-time feedback from medical educators.
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: All active learning and lab sessions and early clinical experience activities are mandatory.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights:
Early Health System Experiences: Students dive into the critical relationship between our partner healthcare system and the community. 

Minimal Lectures, Maximum Engagement: Experiential and active learning in small groups, fostering deep understanding through case-based discussions. 

Integrated Learning: Foundational, clinical, and health system sciences are seamlessly woven together. 

Clinical Learning from Day One: Real-world medicine with patient presentations. 

Community Engagement: Service-learning is embedded throughout the four years. 

Protected Independent Learning Time: Weekly dedicated time for self-directed learning ensures students can explore and grow at their own pace.

State-of-the-Art Facilities: Our cutting-edge simulation center, virtual anatomy lab, ultrasound, and imaging lab. 

AI Integration: Embracing the future, our curriculum includes comprehensive AI education supported technologies, preparing students for the rapidly evolving technological landscape.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: While equipping students with the broad skills needed for primary care medicine, our program offers diverse experiences that include a wide range of medical specialties and health system science instruction throughout the curriculum, preparing students to engage meaningfully in varied community and clinical settings.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: Students will learn foundational research and evidence-based medicine principles. They will effectively locate, analyze, synthesize, and apply medical literature to their own research in an advocacy-driven, patient-centered project that addresses health disparities and promotes equity in underserved communities. In MS1-MS2, students will participate in a scholarly project that is then presented at the end of MS2.
medSchoolCurriculum.academicSystemText: Interdisciplinary foundational, clinical & health system sciences, systems-based courses,  video-captured lectures, small group interactive learning, and clinical application in varied settings.
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: Community service is integrated into service learning, which is a required element of all four years of the curriculum as part of courses and clerkships.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText: All students will be required to complete a community focused scholarly project  by the end of the second year and under the guidance of a faculty member.
medSchoolCurriculum.gradingSystem: The medical school employs a 2-tier Pass/Fail grading system in the pre-clerkship phase of the curriculum and a 4-tier Pass/Fail grading system in the clerkship phase.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: Our class of 64 students will enter a new medical school located on the campus of a large health center dedicated to creating service-oriented physicians with a passion for addressing rural and urban health issues. At MU CFVH School of Medicine, our curriculum utilizes interactive learning through a flipped classroom and clinical presentation approach. Service learning is included as part of the core curriculum.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement: The mission of the Methodist University Cape Fear Valley Health School of Medicine is to prepare our graduates to be socially accountable, community-engaged, evidence-based, compassionate, equity-focused physician leaders who will contribute to mitigating health disparities and improving health outcomes in southeastern NC or wherever they may practice.
medSchoolInformation.videoTitle: Welcome to the Methodist University Cape Fear Valley Health School of Medicine
medSchoolInformation.videoDescription: A welcome message from Dr. Hershey Bell, the Dean of the School of Medicine.

medSchoolApplication.applicantResponseToOffer: 2 weeks, with the window shortening closer to the start of classes.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance:
A minimum of 3 letters (or one committee letter/packet) are required, including at least one from a STEM professor/advisor and one from someone who can speak to your attitude of service. Acceptable sources include: 
-A professor who can speak to your academic abilities
-Physicians you have shadowed or a medical professional for whom you have worked
-A supervisor or employer
-A pre-health advisor

More information here: https://www.methodist.edu/academics/medicine/admissions/recommendations/
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: Candidates rotate between interview stations and are assessed on a variety of competencies.
medSchoolApplication.regionalInterview: A select number of in-person interviews will be available for the 2027 cycle.
medSchoolApplication.videoInterview: The majority of interviews are conducted virtually via Zoom.
medSchoolApplication.secApplSentTo: Applicants who meet minimum admissions criteria
medSchoolApplication.ctsRequired: We do not have an in-state tuition or a residency quota.
medSchoolApplication.acceptOutstateApplInformation: MU CFVH does not require any additional information for out-of-state applicants.
medSchoolApplication.acceptCanadianApplInformation: All candidates must hold US Citizenship or permanent residency and have a bachelor's or advanced degree from a US-accredited institution.
medSchoolApplication.acceptInternationalApplInformation: All candidates must hold US Citizenship or permanent residency and have a bachelor's or advanced degree from a US-accredited institution.
medSchoolApplication.dacaDetail: All candidates must hold US Citizenship or permanent residency and have a bachelor's or advanced degree from a US-accredited institution.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo: Minimum MCAT 500 will be considered for secondary application invitations. During a candidate’s evaluation, the MCAT is a part of the Admissions Committee's comprehensive review, including the number of MCAT attempts and score trends.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScreenAdditionalInfo: A composite score of 500 or higher is the minimum MCAT considered. There are no subsection score requirements, but the Admissions Committee is able to view subsection performance.
medSchoolApplication.gpaScreenAdditionalInfo: MU CFVH requires both a 3.2 total and BCPM GPA for secondary consideration.
medSchoolApplication.minUndergradGpaInfo: Graduate GPAs & coursework are evaluated on a case-by-case basis for consideration if a candidate's undergraduate GPA does not meet our minimum criteria.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: We encourage applicants to upload letters, updates, and other notices via the admissions portal.
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo: Technical standards must be met to matriculate into and progress through the curriculum. After enrollment, Methodist University Cape Fear Valley Health School of Medicine students will review the technical standards each academic year and attest that they continue to meet the following standards with or without reasonable accommodation. At any time, if a new or developing concern arises and an accommodation revision must occur, the student has the right to pursue it with the Student Experience Office.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid:
At the Methodist University Cape Fear Valley Health School of Medicine, we are committed to making medical education accessible and affordable. Our Financial Aid office partners with students to develop individualized funding plans that support both their academic journey and long-term goals. Every student in the first two entering classes will receive a total of $40,000 in tuition remission toward the cost of their medical education, and additional scholarships are available for qualified students.

Students may be eligible for a range of resources, including federal direct loans, private loan options, military and service-based scholarships, and institutional scholarships designed to recognize mission-aligned applicants. We also provide guidance on budgeting, financial literacy, and debt management to help students make informed decisions. 

For additional information on tuition and fees, please visit this webpage: https://www.methodist.edu/academics/medicine/student-experience/aid/.

medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: There is no expiration date for coursework. Candidates with coursework older than 5 years are encouraged to clearly indicate what they have done post-graduation.
